mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.25% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and a fall in the housing starts index (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a divergence between manufacturing strength and housing weakness, which historically precedes equity market pullbacks over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls by more than 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 0.10% during a recession signals a policy-driven liquidity surge, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 0.10% and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters) signals elevated precautionary behavior, which historically coincides with lower consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth > 5% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS grows by more than 5% YoY for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over one month signals a compositional shift in the labor market (e.g., lower-quality jobs replacing higher-quality jobs), which historically precedes equity market underperformance over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0% and UNRATE > 0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index above 4% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which raises interest rate expectations and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 4% YoY for six months.
